description: We are a team of Peruvian geologists passionate about science, exploration, and discovery. We are united by our curiosity about understanding the geological processes of our planet and exploring new frontiers in scientific and space knowledge. We are a collaborative, creative, and committed team, eager to learn, share knowledge, and take on new challenges.
summary: GeoTwin Explorer is an interactive geospatial platform designed to identify and compare terrestrial sites that exhibit characteristics analogous to those observed on the Moon and Mars. It addresses the need to study planetary terrain through comparable terrestrial environments, using Earth-observation data and planetary exploration datasets. The platform incorporates digital elevation models (DEMs), satellite imagery, and analytical tools to connect Earth, the Moon, and Mars through five modules: 3D Atlas, Discover, Compare, Pilot Area, and Data Sources. It includes a catalog of terrestrial field sites and focuses on arid, volcanic, polar, and crater-like environments, positioning the platform as a useful resource for geological and planetary science research.
details:
4. PROJECT DETAILS

4.1. Summary

GeoTwin Explorer is a geospatial analysis tool that links terrestrial geological research with planetary exploration. By integrating satellite-derived information and digital elevation models, it enables users to explore and compare terrain on Earth, the Moon, and Mars using consistent spatial criteria.

Its primary contribution is to make the search for terrestrial analog sites a reproducible process for exploration and preliminary assessment. The platform incorporates measurements, configurable parameters, traceable data sources, and explicit acknowledgment of dataset limitations.

5. PROJECT DESCRIPTION

GeoTwin Explorer is an interactive geospatial platform that enables users to identify, visualize, characterize, and compare terrestrial terrain with regions of interest on the Moon and Mars. It uses topographic, geological, and geomorphological information derived from open scientific data sources.

5.1. What Does GeoTwin Explorer Do, and How Does It Work?

A. 3D Atlas — Planetary Exploration

This module serves as the platform’s entry point. It provides a visual interface for exploring Earth, the Moon, and Mars, examining their surfaces, and identifying geographic and planetary regions of interest.

The initial working catalog includes:

Earth: 20 terrestrial reference sites.

Moon: 17 selected lunar features and regions.

Mars: 11 documented Martian regions.

Exploration provides geological and geomorphological context for the sites of interest and allows users to recognize a range of planetary surface environments.

B. Discover — Identification of Potential Analog Sites

This module is designed to identify features of interest in a lunar or Martian region and relate them to characteristics observable in terrestrial environments.

The attributes considered include:

Crater morphology and circular features.

Volcanic surfaces and lava fields.

Arid plains and sedimentary deposits.

Glacial landforms, permafrost, and potential ice deposits.

Surface roughness, fracturing, and terrain characteristics.

Erosion, sedimentation, and surface-modification processes.

The objective is to support the identification of potential terrestrial analog candidates based on measurable characteristics rather than visual resemblance alone.

C. Compare — Characterization and Similarity Analysis

This module organizes comparisons between a lunar or Martian region and a potential terrestrial analog site. It considers geological, topographic, and geomorphological variables and characteristics, with assistance from AstroBot.

The variables considered include:

Discipline / Parameter Group

Variables of Interest

Topography

Elevation, relative relief, slope, and local terrain.

Geomorphology

Landform morphology, diameter, depth, circularity, and surface roughness.

Geology

Lithology, geologic units, structures, and surficial materials.

Mineralogy

Mineral assemblages and surface composition, where data are available.

Thermal Conditions

Surface temperature and thermal variability.

Environmental Conditions

Aridity, ice, permafrost, and other environmental characteristics.

Operational Considerations

Accessibility, surface stability, and potential hazards or obstacles.

The comparison should identify both similarities and differences between the environments and should not assume that a terrestrial site fully reproduces all planetary conditions.

5.2. DATASETS USED

Dataset

Use and Scope

Reference / Source

NASA JPL — NASADEM HGT v001

Local elevation profiles integrated for 16 terrestrial sites, including the eight sites in Peru. Nominal grid spacing: approximately 30 m; vertical datum: EGM96.

NASA Earthdata / DOI

Copernicus GLO-90 / GLO-30

Terrestrial DEM subsets; the user selects the subset covering the full analysis window. This is a digital surface model (DSM) and may include vegetation and infrastructure.

Copernicus DEM

NASA LOLA and MOLA; USGS HRSC–MOLA and CTX

Global and regional lunar and Martian altimetry. The index records the map projection, nominal resolution, and data subsets.

LOLA; MOLA; USGS Mars data

NASA Earthdata Search

Discovery and selection resource for terrestrial observations by region, date, and variable. The link opens the search interface; it does not select a collection or download a DEM.

NASA Earthdata Search

USGS 3DEP

Hawaiʻi data subset resampled to 100 m for the prepared case studies.

USGS 3DEP

USGS OFR 2007-1089

Geologic polygons for Hawaiʻi at 1:250,000 scale. Coverage does not include Peru.

Publication and data layer

INGEMMET — GEOCATMIN, compiled 1:100,000-scale geology

902 features clipped to the Andahua and Huambo areas at 1:100,000 scale, EPSG:4326. Includes feature identifiers, codes, geologic units, lithologies, and original map-sheet references.

Official service, Layer 11

Natural Earth

Land and lakes mask at 1:50-million scale. Used to constrain regional screening; it is not a substitute for site-scale mapping.

Natural Earth

Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program (GVP)

Georeferenced volcano records. A point location does not represent the full footprint of a volcanic deposit.

Smithsonian GVP

Köppen–Geiger (Beck et al. and others)

Terrestrial climate classification for 1980–2016, derived at approximately 0.083° resolution.

Publication

NSIDC / ILAMB

Circum-Arctic permafrost classification derived at approximately 0.25° resolution. It does not directly measure shallow ground ice.

NSIDC; ILAMB

Planetary surface textures

Mosaics used to guide visual exploration; illumination is illustrative.

NASA Blue Marble; LRO/SVS; Mars/Viking

6. BENEFITS AND IMPACT

GeoTwin Explorer provides benefits across several areas:

Area

Primary Contribution / Impact

Key Tools / Approach

Social

Promotes access to scientific and geospatial knowledge.

Interdisciplinary learning and science communication.

Environmental

Enables the study of extreme environments and geomorphological processes.

Geospatial information without the need for initial physical site disturbance.

Technological

Integrates advanced spatial-analysis tools.

3D visualization, elevation models, geologic mapping, and measurement tools.

Scientific

Supports hypothesis development and comparative analysis.

Study of terrestrial analog sites and surface characteristics.

7. OBJECTIVES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES

7.1. Overall Objective

Develop an interactive geospatial platform to identify, visualize, characterize, and compare terrestrial analog sites for regions on the Moon and Mars using topographic, geological, and geomorphological information from verifiable scientific sources.

7.2. Specific Objectives

Integrate terrestrial and planetary geospatial information from open data sources.

Develop three-dimensional visualization tools.

Implement topographic and morphometric comparison procedures.

Incorporate geologic mapping to characterize terrestrial environments.

Enable area measurements and the export of reproducible results.

8. EXPECTED RESULTS

The intended outcome is a functional web-based platform featuring a catalog of terrestrial and planetary environments, tools for comparing digital elevation models, and capabilities for analyzing and exporting scientific information.

9. DEVELOPMENT METHODOLOGY

The team used a brainstorming process to develop the project concept.

The platform development methodology consists of five stages:

Site and environment identification: selection of terrestrial and planetary terrain based on morphology, geology, slope, and data availability.

Data compilation: integration of digital elevation models, geologic maps, and scientific references.

Geospatial processing: organization and characterization of variables such as elevation, slope, and surface roughness.

Terrain comparison: assessment of similarities and differences at comparable spatial scales and under comparable conditions.

Results documentation: recording of parameters, data sources, measurements, and exportable information.

10. TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

GeoTwin Explorer is being developed as a web-based platform designed to integrate geospatial information and provide an interactive experience for exploring planetary surfaces.

JavaScript has been identified as the programming language, with Visual Studio Code and Visual Studio initially reported as development environments.

The technology architecture and the specific tools used for visualization, data processing, and data management were pending final confirmation by the development team in the project description.

11. CASE STUDIES AND ANALOG-SITE CATALOG

GeoTwin Explorer includes an initial catalog of 20 terrestrial sites, 17 lunar features, and 11 Martian regions selected for their geological and geomorphological significance and their potential for comparative analysis.

The selection includes sites in Peru and international reference locations, allowing the investigation of a range of processes and planetary environments.

11.2. Reference Regions on Mars

Eleven documented Martian regions are included in the catalog, among them:

Arcadia–Amazonis: AP-1, AP-8, and AP-9.

Deuteronilus Mensae.

Jezero Crater.

Meridiani Planum — Eagle.

Polar Plains — Phoenix.

Olympus Mons.

Ulysses Colles.

Gale Crater.

Firsoff Crater.

These regions represent a range of environments and landforms, including arid terrains, volcanic terrains, impact craters, sedimentary deposits, polar surfaces, and potential subsurface ice deposits.

11.3. Prioritization of Demonstration Cases

To demonstrate the platform’s capabilities, the project proposes developing targeted comparisons between a planetary region and a terrestrial candidate site, with justification of the analog relationship and its limitations.

Lunar case study: [ADD LUNAR REGION + TERRESTRIAL SITE + VARIABLES + RESULTS].

Martian case study: [ADD MARTIAN REGION + TERRESTRIAL SITE + VARIABLES + RESULTS].

Featured Peruvian case study: [ADD SITE + RATIONALE + EVIDENCE + RESEARCH CONTRIBUTION].

Identifying new analog sites is a distinguishing feature of the project. Accordingly, established sites used as methodological references must be differentiated from new candidates whose characterization and scientific relevance still need to be demonstrated.

11.4. Technical Information to Be Completed / Confirmed

Component

Technology / Implementation

Programming Language

Modern JavaScript using ES modules. HTML5 and CSS3 for the user interface; Python, PowerShell, and Batch for auxiliary tools and local startup. No specific ECMAScript version is specified.

Development Environment

Visual Studio Code, Node.js, and npm. Use of Visual Studio is not confirmed in the project files.

Frontend Framework

No framework. The interface is built directly with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Includes Progressive Web App (PWA) capabilities.

Geospatial Visualization Libraries

Custom planetary viewer using Canvas 2D and SVG graphics for topographic profiles. Does not use Leaflet, OpenLayers, or Cesium.

3D Visualization Engine

Three.js r160 with WebGL for the astronaut model. Planetary spheres are rendered using a custom spherical renderer in Canvas 2D.

Geospatial Data Processing

Node.js, GeoTIFF.js, Proj4js, Sharp, and PNGJS for elevation-data reading, coordinate transformations, profile sampling, and image preparation.

Mapping Services / APIs

Google Maps in satellite mode, NASA Earthdata/GIBS, Microsoft Planetary Computer, and the Polar Geospatial Center STAC catalog. NASADEM, LOLA, and MOLA provide elevation data.

Backend

No application backend or custom API. Processing is performed in advance and in the browser. Node.js or Python serves files during local execution.

Database

No database management system. The platform uses local JSON files, JavaScript data modules, and binary elevation files.

Hosting and Deployment

GitHub Pages, with a publishing workflow configured through GitHub Actions to deploy the dist directory.

Version Control

Git and GitHub. Repository: GeoTwin-Explorer.
